title: Mid-session plan upgrade: prorate, quota reconciliation, and live-stream billing correctness
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background:
Users can upgrade their account or switch billing plans while an interactive streaming session (WebSocket or server-sent events) is active. Currently, the metering pipeline attributes token usage to the plan that was active at the time of token emission. This produces incorrect outcomes for typical upgrade flows:
- Overcharge: tokens billed to a newly upgraded paid plan remain charged to the previous free/trial bucket when provisional credits were applied, or vice-versa, producing double-charges or orphaned refunds.
- Quota leakage: tokens consumed under a paid plan before a downgrade/upgrade transition may not decrement the new plan's quota, allowing transient bypasses of rate limits.
- Pricing mismatch: model-specific per-token pricing and discount tiers change mid-session and are not reflected in exported invoices or customer-facing usage dashboards.

Goal:
Design and implement a deterministic, auditable reconciliation system that: (1) anchors token attribution to discrete session segments defined by plan change events, (2) retroactively reclassifies provisional credits when necessary, and (3) exposes clear telemetry and customer-facing explanations for any prorations. The solution must preserve SLOs for streaming latency and avoid blocking the runtime.

Requirements / Acceptance Criteria:
- When a plan change event occurs mid-session, the metering pipeline creates a new session segment with a stable ledger anchor. All subsequent token emissions are tagged with the new segment id.
- Tokens emitted prior to the plan change are either left as-is or reclassified according to a deterministic policy (see Policies below). Reclassification must be idempotent and visible in the audit ledger.
- Billing exports (invoiceable records) must reflect per-segment pricing, discounts, and quota consumption. Exports must be consistent with the runtime ledger within 1 minute of the upgrade event under normal conditions.
- Quota enforcement must consider per-segment reservations: an upgrade should optionally draw from a paid quota immediately and not allow short-term quota circumvention by rapid plan toggles.
- Rollback safety: in case of transient errors during reconciliation, the system should support safe retry without duplicate billing (idempotent reconciler).

Policies (initial proposal):
- Upgrade path (free -> paid): mark a hard boundary. Tokens emitted after the upgrade time are billed to the paid segment. Any provisional free-tier credits applied to in-flight tokens remain on the free segment; however, if a later reconciliation finds that a free-tier provisional credit was incorrectly applied due to caching/duplication, the reconciler will move the credit to the paid segment and emit an adjustment line in the ledger.
- Downgrade path (paid -> free): allow a configurable grace window (default 30s) where paid quota remains reserved for the session. After the window, subsequent tokens get billed to the free segment. If revoke is requested, reconcile and prorate by token counts.
- Rapid toggles: if a plan toggles more than N times in M seconds (configurable), the user is rate-limited from further toggles for a cooldown to prevent abuse of quota transitions.

Technical design (high level):
- Event model: implement a "session-segment" event emitted when plan change is confirmed. This event contains: session_id, segment_id, plan_id, effective_ts, prev_segment_id. Keep payload small.
- Ledger anchoring: the metering pipeline must persist a compact marker (segment_id, effective_ts) in the same ordering store used for token ledger anchors to guarantee determinism on replay.
- Token tagging: streaming worker attaches current segment_id to token debit events as they are emitted; tags are used downstream by aggregator and exporter to group by segment.
- Reconciler: a separate background job scans segments and applies reclassification rules. It produces idempotent adjustment entries in the ledger (negative + positive entries) with references to original token batches and a reconciliation_reason code.
- Exports & UI: expand invoice and usage export schema to include segment_id and plan_name. Console usage page will show a per-session timeline with plan change markers and prorated adjustments.

Testing & Validation:
- Unit tests for segment event creation and token tagging.
- Integration tests: simulated WebSocket sessions that upgrade/downgrade mid-stream with deterministic random seeds. Validate ledger invariants (sum of per-segment debits equals end-to-end token delta after reconciliation).
- Load tests: create 5k concurrent streaming sessions with 2% performing plan changes mid-session; ensure median token tagging latency < 5ms and reconciler can catch up in < 60s for normal load.
- Audit harness: end-to-end shadow-run on staging over a 48-hour window comparing existing billing exporter and reconciled exporter; produce discrepancy report.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature-flag initial segment tagging and ledger anchoring. Deploy to internal orgs and opt-in customers.
2) Run reconciler in dry-run mode and surface adjustments in internal dashboards.
3) Enable adjustment writes for a small percentage of customers. Monitor refunds/adjustments.
4) Full rollout and update public billing docs and UI help text.

Telemetry & Alerting:
- New metrics: segment_events/sec, reconciliation_rate, reconciliation_latency_p50/p95, segment_reclassifications, invoice_adjustments_count.
- Alerts: reconciliation backlog > 5 minutes; reconciliation error rate > 0.1%; mismatch between exporter and runtime ledger > 0.05% of tokens.

Security & Compliance:
- All adjustment entries must be signed/anchored to immutable ledger snapshots for auditability.
- Ensure PII-free logs and redact sensitive plan metadata as needed.

Open questions / Tradeoffs:
- Should we allow client-provided 'effective_ts' when plan change is triggered from SDK vs. server-authoritative time? (Prefer server-authoritative to avoid clock skew abuse).
- Pricing impact: do we apply prorate refunds at token granularity or time-slice granularity? Token granularity is fairer but more expensive to compute.
- How to handle model-switch+plan-switch simultaneously? We'll treat them as independent orthogonal segments for now but document interactions.

References:
- RFC: /docs/prd/billing/mid-session-proration.md (internal)
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4123
